name: butcher knife
summary: One bloodied butcher knife, carried in the character-left hand as a costume piece, never used on anything. No second blade, no sheath.

draw.shape: A broad rectangular butcher blade tapering to a point, with a straight spine and a short riveted handle. The blade is about as long as the character's own forearm and clearly wider than the handle, so the silhouette reads as a blade at cell size.
draw.material: Dull steel with a lightly specular edge and a dark riveted wooden handle. A few dried dark-red smears and one thin drip line sit on the flat of the blade, #7A1B1B with #3F0D0D in shadow, on the blade only.
draw.readability: The blade stays a distinct flat shape against the costume, edge and point legible in every frame, never a smudge, a stub, or a shape that merges into the body behind it.

hands.character-left: The fist wraps the handle behind the rivets, fingers closed, thumb along the spine. The blade points down and slightly forward, away from the body.

hold.orientation: The handle leads at the hand and the point trails below it. The blade never points at the viewer, at the character's own face or body, or straight up.
hold.rest: Hanging at the character-left side, blade down and angled slightly away from the leg, unless the set below says otherwise.

carriage.dance: Swings loosely with the character-left arm on the beat, blade down, the point kept clear of the body and the costume.
carriage.sing: Held low and out to the character-left side, blade down, well away from the face and the microphone.
carriage.flinch: Stays still at the side through the reaction, blade down.
carriage.guard: Drops low and angles away from the body while the free arm shields, blade down and never crossing the face.
carriage.entrance: Lifted once in a small, bashful greeting, blade still down, then settled at the side.
carriage.victory: Rises with the celebration, held up by the handle with the blade angled away from the head, never overhead point-down.
carriage.ko: Hangs slack at the character-left side, point toward the floor.

never: in the character-right hand, or swapped between hands across a set
raised, cocked or swung in a stabbing, slashing or striking action
pointed at the viewer, at another figure, or at the character's own face or body
touching anyone, anything, or the floor
dripping, spattering or leaving blood on the character, the costume, the glove or the ground
a second blade, a sheath, a cleaver, a machete or an axe
replaced by a bare fist, an open hand or an empty hand in any frame, whatever the arm is doing
